hero.subtitle: Not three libraries that look alike. One specification, implemented idiomatically in each language — and proven by the same test fixture running in all of them.

problem.title: Your stack speaks three languages. Your logs speak three dialects.
problem.lead: A request crosses your Node gateway, your Python worker and your .NET service.
body: Three loggers. Three ways of masking a credit card. Three names for the same correlation id. Three answers to “what happens when the log sink goes down”.
Correlating that request means reconciling three different truths — by hand, at 3 a.m., while someone waits.

matrix.title: SyntropyLog
matrix.subtitle: Declarative PII masking, context that survives async boundaries, and a logging path that never throws — in the languages your stack already uses.

principles.title: How we think about observability
principles.subtitle: Four decisions that are already in the code. They are why the implementations agree — and why, where they don't, they don't by choice.

items.title: The logging path never throws
items.body: If your logger can crash your request handler, it is not an observability tool — it is a new failure mode. A failure goes to a hook and a counter. Never to your caller.

items.title: A masking strategy is data, not code
items.body: Adding a strategy shouldn't mean writing the same function in four languages. It is a spec the engine interprets — which is why the output can be identical everywhere.

items.title: Wire names belong to your services, not to us
items.body: Your gateway calls it x-request-id and the legacy service calls it X-Correlation. Each service declares its own map and the id survives the translation. Headers don't have to agree.

items.title: Parity is proven by a test, not by a document
items.body: The same seventeen masking cases — literally the same file, byte for byte — run in the Node, Python and Java suites. If an implementation drifts, its build turns red.

getStarted.title: Start with your language
getStarted.subtitle: Install it, and the defaults already mask passwords, tokens, emails and card numbers.
getStarted.footnote: Every implementation is Apache 2.0 and has zero required runtime dependencies.
